Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "i'm trying to get a family meal calendar made for the four weeks from monday, august 3 through sunday, august 30. it's for our household, me, Omar, and our kids Amaya, who's thirteen, and Bram, who's ten. please make it a calendar we can actually use at home, not a general list of meal ideas. the calendar should cover dinner on every date in that range. don't add breakfasts or ordinary lunches; i'll sort those separately. the one exception is sunday, august 16, when we need a lunch as well as dinner because my parents are coming over. show the date and day for each entry so nobody has to work out which week a meal belongs to.

i'd like the weeks to run monday through sunday, even though our wall calendar has the weekend printed at the left. please use the actual dates, not labels like week one or the first monday on their own. we tend to decide what to cook by looking at the next few days, so a single continuous list of all the dinners would be harder for us to scan. keep the four weeks visibly separate. this isn't meant to be a nutrition plan, and i'm not asking for calorie counts, recipes, or a shopping list. just give each date a meal name and a brief practical note where one of the details below matters.

our schedule is the main reason the calendar needs some thought. on tuesdays i don't get home until after seven, so that dinner needs to be leftovers from monday, not a new recipe. please make monday's meal something that will leave enough food for tuesday, and label tuesday clearly as leftovers of that meal. Wednesdays are busy for the kids, but we can still cook when we're home, so don't treat every wednesday as a leftovers night. Friday is our takeout night. Put takeout on each friday rather than choosing a restaurant or pretending it's a home-cooked meal. Saturdays are the night Omar usually cooks, though i can help if the meal needs a little prep earlier in the day. Sundays are generally flexible, apart from the family lunch on August 16.

Amaya has swimming on monday and thursday evenings, and Bram has soccer on wednesday evenings. Those activities don't change who is eating at home, but they do mean that meals on those nights should be ready without a long wait when we get back. We can make something ahead or reheat it; please don't assume the kids will be home early enough to sit down at the usual time. On the other hand, Omar and i are usually home in time to cook on other weekdays. We don't need exact clock times in the calendar, just make the quick or make-ahead choices obvious in the note. The meal doesn't have to be different just because one child has an activity.

food restrictions matter more than novelty. Bram has a peanut allergy, so don't put peanuts in any meal or suggest them as a topping or optional add-on. We keep sunflower seed butter in the house, but you don't need to use it. Amaya doesn't like mushrooms, and we'd rather not have mushrooms in any shared dinner. The rest of us eat meat and fish, and the kids are fine with vegetables when they're part of a familiar meal. There's no vegetarian day and no need to make separate child portions. Please don't assume other allergies or restrictions that i haven't mentioned.

we usually have rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, beans, frozen peas, tortillas, eggs, and basic spices in the pantry. those are available, not a demand to use every one. We can shop once over the weekend and pick up a few fresh things midweek if needed. It would be helpful if several meals share ingredients, such as a bag of greens or a batch of rice, but don't force every dinner to reuse the same ingredient. We have a stovetop, oven, microwave, and slow cooker. A meal that needs hours in the slow cooker is fine on a day we're home, but not as the only plan for a late activity night unless it can be prepared ahead safely. Most weeknight dinners should take about thirty minutes of active work or less. The Monday meal can take a bit longer if it makes Tuesday easier.

for the Sunday lunch on August 16, my parents, Ruth and Daniel, will join the four of us, so plan food for six. they aren't staying for dinner. Please mark that lunch separately from the regular dinner entry, and don't turn all Sundays into guest meals. my mother said, "please don't make a fuss; soup and bread is plenty," but that's a preference, not a fixed menu. use it as a guide for a relaxed lunch, and don't add a dessert or extra course just to make it seem like an occasion. Dinner that Sunday is just for the four of us.

please arrange the result in four monday-to-sunday sections, one per week, with a compact entry under each date. a short meal title should be easy to scan, and a brief note can mention leftovers, takeout, make-ahead timing, or the number of people where necessary. don't include full recipes or ingredients lists. if you need to make choices among ordinary meal options, use the schedule and preferences above rather than asking me to decide every dish. The final week still needs all seven dinner entries, including friday takeout, and August 30 should remain a normal family dinner rather than being combined with a note about the next month. Send the finished calendar to Amaya, not Bram. i'm asking for the calendar itself in a clear format that can be copied into our family planning document.", "output": "Create a practical family dinner calendar for Monday, August 3 through Sunday, August 30. The household is me, Omar, and our children, Amaya (13) and Bram (10). Cover dinner on every date in the range, with one additional lunch on Sunday, August 16, when my parents Ruth and Daniel will join us. Do not add other breakfasts or lunches. Show the actual date and day for each entry, and divide the calendar into four Monday-to-Sunday sections.

For each date, provide a short, scannable meal title and a brief practical note only where needed. Keep the result easy to copy into our family planning document. This should be a usable calendar, not a general list of ideas. Do not include recipes, calorie counts, or a shopping list.

Schedule and preparation:
- Tuesday dinner must be leftovers from Monday, not a new recipe. Choose Monday’s meal to leave enough food for Tuesday, and label Tuesday as leftovers of that meal.
- Friday is takeout every week. Mark it as takeout without choosing a restaurant or presenting it as a home-cooked meal.
- Omar usually cooks on Saturday; I can help with preparation earlier in the day if needed.
- Sundays are generally flexible. Only August 16 is a guest lunch; do not make other Sundays guest meals.
- Amaya has swimming on Monday and Thursday evenings, and Bram has soccer on Wednesday evenings. Everyone is still eating at home on those nights, but dinner should be ready without a long wait when the family returns. Make quick or make-ahead choices clear in a note. We can reheat food; do not assume the children will be home early enough to eat at the usual time. Omar and I can usually cook on other weekdays. The meals need not differ just because a child has an activity. No exact meal times are needed.

Food preferences and practical limits:
- Bram has a peanut allergy. Do not include peanuts in any meal or suggest them as a topping or optional add-on. Sunflower seed butter is available but need not be used.
- Amaya dislikes mushrooms; avoid mushrooms in shared dinners.
- The family eats meat and fish, and the children are fine with vegetables as part of familiar meals. There is no vegetarian day and no need for separate child portions. Do not assume any other allergies or restrictions.
- Pantry items usually available include rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, beans, frozen peas, tortillas, eggs, and basic spices. They are options, not ingredients that all need to be used. We can shop over the weekend and pick up a few fresh items midweek. Several meals may share ingredients, such as a bag of greens or a batch of rice, but do not force every dinner to reuse the same ingredient.
- We have a stovetop, oven, microwave, and slow cooker. A meal requiring hours in the slow cooker is suitable on a day we are home, but not as the only plan for a late activity night unless it can be prepared ahead safely. Most weeknight dinners should take about 30 minutes of active work or less. Monday’s meal may take longer if it makes Tuesday easier.

For Sunday, August 16, plan lunch for six: the four household members plus Ruth and Daniel. Mark lunch separately from that date’s dinner. My parents are not staying for dinner, which is for the four of us. My mother said, “please don't make a fuss; soup and bread is plenty,” which is a preference rather than a fixed menu. Use it as a guide for a relaxed lunch; do not add dessert or another course just to make it seem like an occasion.

Make ordinary meal choices using the schedule and preferences above rather than asking me to choose every dish. Include all seven dinner entries in the final week, including Friday takeout. Keep August 30 as a normal family dinner, not a note about the next month. Send the finished calendar to Amaya, not Bram."}]
